source.title: Grounding Representation Similarity with Statistical Testing
source.authors: Frances Ding; Jean-Stanislas Denain; Jacob Steinhardt

record.tranche_reason: The study directly compares representation dissimilarity measures, finds that their judgments can differ, and reports settings where they fail to track functional differences. It refines how representation similarity should be evaluated rather than testing convergence with model scale.
record.gate_note: The paper measures distances across model seeds, layers, and principal-component deletions and relates distances to probing or out-of-distribution performance. It also reports metric-specific results in figures and tables. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study shows that CCA-, CKA- and Procrustes-based measures disagree on whether BERT models differing only in seed learn similar representations (Fig. 1). It also shows that CKA's small cross-seed distance reflects insensitivity to all but the top principal components (Fig. 2). This bears directly on V6 and, under each metric, on V3. Most of the paper (Table 1) scores metric validity against functional differences, which is not a convergence measurement.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also stress that the metrics disagree on whether seed-differing networks learn similar representations. They add that some of the sensitivity to seed tracks real functional (OOD) differences, so the intuition that seeds give 'similar' representations needs refinement.
record.recipe_differences: The study benchmarks linear CKA, CCA-derived measures, and Orthogonal Procrustes against functional behavior; it does not reproduce either original source's method or claim. It evaluates several metrics rather than testing scale-driven convergence.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by metric, model modality, layer, and functional benchmark. For BERT seed comparisons, PWCCA, CKA, and Procrustes differ in sensitivity; for PC deletion, the distance detection threshold differs markedly by metric. Correlation with OOD accuracy is much lower on BERT medium Numerical and ResNet CIFAR-10C tasks than on the HANS benchmark.

fits_no_version.finding: Representation dissimilarity across seeds correlates with functional differences: probe accuracy (ρ up to 0.905) and HANS OOD accuracy (ρ≈0.55). Correlations are near zero for the Numerical stress test and CIFAR-10C.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Seed-induced representational differences are partly functionally meaningful, and metrics vary in how well they track them.

record.problems: The study covers a limited set of architectures, models, and functional behaviors. Several similarity-distance findings are presented qualitatively in figures rather than with extractable numerical distances. Some reported p-values assume independence despite correlated randomness; the authors warn these are invalid and may overstate significance. PWCCA could not be computed for the vision experiments because n < d.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. The table rows use the paper's aggregate summaries; individual layer-by-layer results and individual CIFAR-10C corruption correlations are not separate rows here because they expand the same reported benchmark conditions.

untested.parts: No scale sweep and no cross-architecture comparison.
No identification of shared features or subspaces, or of unit/basis differences. Only same-architecture BERT base seed pairs (5 pairs) are compared.
Procrustes is used only as a distance; mapping loss, stitching and relative representations are not tested.
Neighbour count (k) and representations computed on OOD inputs are not varied.
No plateau analysis and no data/objective attribution.

missing.what: First-layer PC-deletion thresholds per metric versus the seed baseline
Numerical cross-seed vs within-model distance values per metric (figure only)

record.verdict_notes: Most of the record's rows measure metric validity rather than convergence, so they were unlinked. The V6 support rests on Section 3's figure-based contrasts, stated in the text with no numeric distances.

versions.untested_parts: No scaling sweep or comparison of independently trained models across size or capability.
Tests representation distances across random seeds for same-architecture models, but does not identify shared features or subspaces, or test whether individual units/bases differ.

Orthogonal Procrustes is used as a distance measure; the paper does not test whether mapped representations are interchangeable with little loss, or test stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified across models.
Tests several distance measures and input/task settings, but does not vary neighbour count or test out-of-distribution input data for representation-distance robustness as such.
Does not test whether convergence plateaus or whether shared training data/objectives explain alignment rather than a shared model of reality.

rows.stage_stated: pretrained, not finetuned for particular tasks
rows.operation_detail: Computed representation dissimilarities and correlated them with differences in QNLI probing accuracy across pretraining seeds and layer depth.
rows.measure: Spearman ρ and Kendall τ rank correlation between dissimilarity and probing-accuracy difference; Procrustes ρ=0.862, τ=0.670; CKA ρ=0.876, τ=0.685; PWCCA ρ=0.763, τ=0.564.
rows.value: See measure; all three reported metric correlations are positive.
rows.note: Aggregate benchmark result; the paper reports one summary per metric for the benchmark.
rows.check: Rank correlation of a dissimilarity measure with probe-accuracy differences evaluates the metric's validity. It is not a level of cross-seed convergence, so it bears on no version.

rows.subject: BERT base models (two-model comparison, averaged over 5 pairs)
rows.size_stated: BERT base: 12 hidden layers of 768 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Compared each layer's representation to layers in the same model and a second model using PWCCA.

conditions.value: layer 7 of Model A compared with layers in both models

rows.measure: PWCCA distances: the layer-7 representation in the other model was farther away than every other layer in Model A; the paper says random initialization can outweigh large changes in layer depth.
rows.baseline: Distances to other layers in Model A
rows.value: Figure only; layer 7 in the other model farther than any layer in Model A
rows.note: Authors describe this as PWCCA failing specificity to random initialization.
rows.check: State 'reversed' is wrong. For V6 the metric disagreement is observed. For V3, PWCCA rates the corresponding layer in a different-seed model farther than any same-model layer, so convergence reads only partial under PWCCA, not reversed.

source_check.correct: V3: partial under PWCCA; V6: observed metric dependence when compared with r11–r12. PWCCA describes cross-seed representations as quite dissimilar, with corresponding layer 7 farther apart than any within-model layer comparison.
source_check.problem: The single observed state fits V6 but overstates convergence under PWCCA for V3.

rows.subject: BERT base models (two-model comparison, averaged over 5 pairs)
rows.size_stated: BERT base: 12 hidden layers of 768 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Compared layer-7 representation distances within one model and across a second model using CKA.
rows.measure: CKA distances; the paper states CKA can distinguish layer 7 in the other model from layers 4 or 10 in the same model.
rows.baseline: Distances to layers 4 and 10 in the same model
rows.value: Figure only; cross-model layer 7 is distinguishable from same-model layers 4 and 10
rows.note: Qualitative comparison; the paper describes CKA as having better specificity to random initialization than PWCCA.
rows.check: Under CKA, the corresponding cross-seed layer is closer than same-model layers 3 away, so V3 is observed under CKA. The row is also part of the V6 contrast. State should be observed, not partial.

rows.subject: BERT base models (two-model comparison, averaged over 5 pairs)
rows.size_stated: BERT base: 12 hidden layers of 768 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Compared distances between corresponding and non-corresponding layers using Orthogonal Procrustes.
rows.measure: Orthogonal Procrustes distances; the paper says it distinguishes layers once they are 4–5 layers apart, with smaller but non-trivial specificity to random initialization.
rows.baseline: Distance between corresponding layers across models
rows.value: Figure only; layers 4–5 apart are distinguishable
rows.check: Under Procrustes, cross-seed corresponding layers are closer only than layers 4–5 apart. V3 is partial; the row is part of the V6 contrast.

source_check.correct: V3: partial; V6: observed metric dependence when compared with r10–r11. Orthogonal Procrustes has smaller but nontrivial specificity, distinguishing layers separated by 4–5 layers.
source_check.problem: The partial state fits V3 but should be distinguished from the observed metric dependence supporting V6.

rows.subject: Pretrained BERT base (layer 12)
rows.size_stated: BERT base: 12 hidden layers of 768 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Deleted smallest principal components and measured CKA distance against the original representation.
rows.measure: CKA distance exceeded the random-initialization distance baseline only after deleting 97% of components; probing accuracy then fell from 80% to 63% (chance 50%).
rows.baseline: Average distance between networks trained with different random seeds; probing chance 50%
rows.note: Text states the threshold and accuracy drop; the plotted distance values themselves are not given numerically.
rows.check: CKA needs 97% of PCs deleted to exceed the seed-distance baseline. Its 'similar across seeds' verdict rests on top-PC dominance, which is metric dependence.

rows.check: Procrustes threshold is about 85%. Read jointly with r13 and r15 as a cross-metric contrast.

relationships.condition: BERT base pretrained with different seeds; PWCCA vs CKA vs Orthogonal Procrustes
relationships.reason: Metrics disagree on cross-seed similarity (r10–r12). CKA's small seed distance reflects insensitivity: 97% PC deletion is needed vs about 55% for PWCCA (r13–r15).
relationships.display_finding: CKA, PWCCA and orthogonal Procrustes disagreed on cross-seed similarity, with CKA requiring 97% principal-component deletion versus about 55% for PWCCA to register changes.

relation.reason: Its own BERT experiments compare cross-seed representations under multiple measures and test those measures against functional differences.

tranche.reason: The study directly demonstrates metric-dependent readings of cross-seed convergence and argues that intuitive expectations about seed similarity need qualification.

source_check.notes: Figure 1 findings are qualitative averages over five BERT-base model pairs. Section 4.1 shows that some sensitivity to seed differences tracks real OOD functional differences; similarity rankings do not quantify how many features are shared.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: BERT base models differing only in pretraining seed; measured with the tested similarity metrics
reader_labels.reason: The seed comparison is metric-dependent: PWCCA treats the different-seed corresponding layer as farther away than other layers in the same network, while CKA and Procrustes show different degrees of layer specificity (r10–r12). These results do not establish shared features or subspaces.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: BERT base seed comparisons and principal-component deletion; tested metrics
reader_labels.reason: The measures give different judgments of seed and layer differences, and require substantially different levels of component deletion to reach the seed-distance baseline (r10–r15).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.reason: Metric correlations vary with task and setting and are low for Numerical stress-test accuracy and CIFAR-10C corruption accuracy, despite positive correlations in other benchmarks (r1–r9).
